title: Chapter 3
text: novel (n.), a small tale, generally of love from Samuel Johnson’s Dictionary of the English Language (1755) jung ftak (n.), a Persian bird, the male of which had only one wing, on the right side, and the female only one wing, on the left side; instead of the missing wings, the male had a hook of bone, and the female an eyelet of bone, and it was by uniting hook and eye that they were enabled to fly – each, when alone, had to remain on the ground from Webster’s Twentieth Century Dictionary of the English Language (1943)
